changes: All clips in a pack now get the same perceived loudness. Measured over 28 packs the volume spread dropped from 5.1 dB to 0.6 dB, which is quieter than handmade packs vary. The old modes are still there in the export settings.
The peak limit went from 0.93 to 0.89, so clips no longer clip after they are encoded.

Still images: if the frame at the start of a line is black, a blend or needlessly blurry, Voicitool takes a better frame from the same shot. Bad frames went from 2.3 to 0.4 percent, and the image never jumps to a different shot.
Picking a pack or a recording from the game now has a search box, shows the details on the right and starts only when you press Start. Recordings that already have a video are marked.
While something loads there is a loading bar instead of German text.
The new texts are translated into all 26 languages.

From the game: Voicitool now also finds packs whose lines are stored as .txt files and packs that sit inside a collection folder. Recordings that ended with "the recordings do not match any line of this pack" now work.

The picker for packs and recordings opens right away and fills in while it loads. Reading the recordings takes about a quarter of a second instead of eleven, and it shows the game folder. The finished video shows its full path.
The export folder is now sorted into "Zips", "Ordner" and "Exportierte Videos". What is already there is moved into place once.
Provided lyrics are now stored with the video in the inbox, so they survive a restart. The editor says whether they were used, and if they were not, why.

Pack import fixes: a pack video without an audio track no longer fails, a pack without any timestamp is rejected with a clear message, leftover entries no longer create empty lines, and icon, subtitle and description are taken over.
The texts of the new features are translated into all 26 languages.

New: edit a finished pack. "From the game" on the start page takes a dub pack from Choicer Voicer and turns it into a project with video, lines, speakers and timings. Nothing is recognized again, it takes a few seconds and needs no graphics card.
New: turn a recording session into a video. Pick a session you recorded, alone or with friends, and Voicitool lays the recordings over the pack video and saves one video file you can share.
Lines now end a bit sooner after the last word and speaker changes may move across slightly longer words. Measured on 28 human made packs, 10 packs got better and none got worse.
Lines that consist only of an outro phrase like "thanks for watching" are dropped. Speech recognition likes to hear those in music.

Fixed: cutting the video could lose repeats when the line they came from was cut away, could export at the wrong frame rate with duplicated frames, and let picture and sound drift apart by up to one frame per cut.

Fixed in the editor: moving a line sideways could silently give it to another speaker, splitting could create a line that is too short or has no text, splitting a line with repeats now gives the repeats their own recording, and deleting a line no longer leaves ghost repeats behind.

Process online: quiet moments without words, like gasping or sighing, now become a placeholder line, the same way processing on your PC already did. In a test episode this turned 18 missed lines into none.
Process online: the preview video is now made while the separation service is working. For a 12 minute episode that saves about two and a half minutes.
The preview video is now also encoded by Intel and AMD graphics, not only NVIDIA.
Online jobs only switch to the processor when the graphics card is really full. Before, a busy graphics card made the laugh detection about 20 times slower.

Several fixes in online processing: lines could overlap when a service reported times beyond the piece it was given, long stretches without a pause were not cut into pieces, Gemini could stop with a technical error or quietly return nothing, and waiting in the MVSEP queue no longer triggers a wrong warning about the graphics card.
The preview video no longer keeps being encoded in the background when processing fails.

Lines now end closer to the last word instead of running about a tenth of a second too long. Measured against 27 human made packs, the lines match theirs better and cut off slightly fewer word endings. This applies to newly processed videos.

Splitting a line now cuts in the pause between two words instead of in the middle of one, and it matches the words of the text to the recognized words. Before, a word could end up in the wrong half, especially after the text had been edited.
Process online: the audio is now sent for speech recognition in one minute pieces. That is clearly more accurate, in our tests Groq and Cloudflare were as accurate as the recognition on your PC.
The service list now says what each service is good at, based on these tests: Groq is the fastest, Cloudflare just as accurate, Gemini clearly less accurate with a small daily limit.
While waiting in the MVSEP queue, Voicitool shows about how long it takes and how many jobs are ahead.
If the graphics card is busy (for example with a game), online jobs work out speakers and laughs on the processor instead.
When a service's per minute limit is reached, Voicitool waits briefly and tries again.
Fixed: the search in "Provide text" could take minutes for YouTube videos, because it loaded the automatic translations of the subtitles in about 100 languages.

Process online: PCs without a suitable graphics card can let free online services separate the voices (MVSEP) and recognize the text (Groq, Cloudflare or Gemini). Set it up under Settings → Process online, a step by step guide with links is included. Voicitool asks once at start, and a new "Process online" button sits next to "Process" in the inbox.
If you set up more than one service, pick the one for each video right next to the button. The list shows the model and which one is recommended.
When you download from YouTube, tick "Also get subtitles" and the uploader's subtitles are added to the video as provided text right away.
Subtitles now become one line per subtitle instead of breaking sentences where the subtitle wrapped.
Fixed: "Background" and "Voices only" could stay silent in the player while the PC was busy, for example during an export.
Background volume: a slider under Export → Background and right in the player sets how loud the background is. The exported pack uses the same setting.
New "Background + voices" button in the player when you use your own instrumental: your instrumental together with the separated voices.
Your own instrumental now gets the same loudness as the music in the video. Before, it could end up louder, especially in songs.
Align by hand: listening stays exactly in sync when you move the instrumental or zoom while it plays.
Downloads (videos, instrumentals, AI models) no longer wait for a running export.
The progress of processing, exports and downloads now also shows in the Voicitool icon in the taskbar.
When a video link can't be reached, the error now says so instead of talking about AI models.
The new "Provide text" window is now translated into all app languages.

Provide text: before processing, give Voicitool the lyrics, the script or the subtitles. It searches subtitles in the video file, YouTube subtitles, LRCLIB, lyrics.ovh and Fandom episode transcripts, or you paste the text yourself. Voicitool then uses its spelling and fills in missing words.
Cut video: in the editor you can now cut parts out of the video. The original stays untouched, the cut parts are skipped while playing and left out of the pack.
Align the instrumental by hand: see the separated background and your own instrumental as two waveforms, drag yours into place and listen to one of them or both at once.
If you set your own instrumental, "Background" in the editor now plays that one.
The automatic instrumental alignment no longer gets thrown off by single wrong matches.
Where two lines touch, the middle of the edge moves both lines, left or right of it only one. The mouse pointer shows which.
Repeats can now be linked and unlinked by hand in the right-click menu.
Fixed: the video jumped by one pixel when the subtitle line changed, and character names were translated when switching the app language.

Fewer invented lines: the speech recognition likes to "hear" "Thank you." or "Tschüss" in music or silence. These are now dropped when the recognition itself is unsure about them. On 25 test videos this removed about a fifth of all invented lines.

Better speaker detection in long videos with many characters: short snippets no longer pile up into extra "characters" that mix several voices. In a test episode with 10 characters, Voicitool now finds exactly 10 instead of 17.

New Voicitool.exe: Windows Defender wrongly flagged the previous one as "Trojan:Win32/Wacatac.B!ml". The new exe drops a start option that virus scanners often dislike and has been reported to Microsoft as a false alarm.
Faster speech recognition on PCs without an NVIDIA graphics card: it now uses all processor cores instead of four.
The setup now always installs the x64 version of Python, so it should also work on Windows laptops with an ARM processor (for example Snapdragon). Not tested on such a laptop yet.
Voicitool now reports once a day that it is in use (only "active" and the build number), so I can see roughly how many people use it. You can switch this off under Settings, Updates.
First public version on GitHub.
Voicitool and the setup now start in your Windows language. The setup language can be changed at the top right.
Updates can be installed from inside the app: a note appears at the top when a new version is out.
After starting, the small start window stays until Voicitool is ready and then brings it to the front.
After an update, the installation is checked in the background instead of opening the whole setup.
A failed update no longer blocks the start. Voicitool then simply starts the version you already have.
